enhanced.fullText:
The New Jersey Veterans Tuition Benefits program, established under N.J.S.A. 18A:62-6, provides comprehensive educational support to qualified veterans and their dependents attending eligible New Jersey institutions of higher education. This regulation outlines the administration, eligibility criteria, application procedures, and institutional responsibilities for implementing this vital student service benefit.

Eligibility for New Jersey Veterans Tuition Benefits extends to veterans who were legal residents of New Jersey at the time of their initial entry into military service and have maintained such residency, or who have become New Jersey residents and have resided in the state for at least one year immediately preceding enrollment. The program covers veterans who served in the Armed Forces of the United States, including the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines, Space Force, and Coast Guard, during specified periods of conflict or peacekeeping operations as designated by federal law.

Qualified veterans must have received an honorable discharge or be currently serving in good standing. The benefit extends to certain dependents, including spouses and children of veterans who died as a result of service-connected disabilities, prisoners of war, or those declared missing in action. Dependent children must be under age 26 and unmarried to maintain eligibility, with certain exceptions for active military service interruptions.

The tuition benefit covers the full cost of tuition and approved fees at New Jersey public institutions of higher education, including county colleges, state colleges and universities, and Rutgers University. For students attending eligible private institutions within New Jersey, the benefit provides tuition assistance equivalent to the highest tuition charged at New Jersey public research universities, with the student responsible for any remaining balance.

Institutional responsibilities include establishing clear application procedures, maintaining accurate records of veteran student enrollment and benefit utilization, and providing appropriate academic and student support services. Institutions must designate qualified personnel to serve as veterans' education certifying officials who are knowledgeable about both state and federal veterans' education benefits. These officials must complete required training programs and maintain current certification through the State Approving Agency.

Application procedures require veterans to submit DD-214 discharge documentation, proof of New Jersey residency, and completed state veterans' tuition benefit application forms. Dependent applicants must provide additional documentation establishing their relationship to the qualifying veteran and proof of the veteran's service-connected death, prisoner of war status, or missing in action designation. All applications must be submitted with supporting documentation at least 60 days prior to the beginning of the academic term for which benefits are requested.

Institutions must verify student eligibility, academic progress, and enrollment status each semester. Students receiving veterans' tuition benefits must maintain satisfactory academic progress as defined by institutional standards and federal financial aid regulations. Failure to maintain academic standards may result in suspension or termination of benefits, with provisions for appeal and reinstatement under specified circumstances.

Coordination with other veterans' benefits, including federal GI Bill programs, requires careful management to ensure compliance with all applicable regulations while maximizing student benefit utilization. Institutions must provide clear guidance to veteran students regarding the interaction between state and federal benefits and assist in optimizing benefit usage for degree completion.

The program includes provisions for summer session coverage, graduate study continuation, and transfer between eligible institutions within New Jersey. Students may utilize benefits for undergraduate and graduate degree programs, certificate programs, and approved workforce development initiatives that lead to industry-recognized credentials.

Recordkeeping requirements mandate that institutions maintain comprehensive files for each veteran student, including all eligibility documentation, enrollment verification records, academic progress reports, and benefit payment records. These records must be retained for a minimum of five years following the student's last enrollment and made available for state audit purposes.

Institutions must establish appeal procedures for veterans whose benefits are denied, suspended, or terminated. These procedures must provide due process protections, including written notification of adverse decisions, opportunity for hearing, and right to representation. Appeals must be resolved within specified timeframes to minimize disruption to students' educational progress.

Quality assurance measures require regular program evaluation, including tracking of veteran student success metrics, graduation rates, employment outcomes, and benefit utilization patterns. Institutions must participate in statewide data collection efforts and submit required reports to the New Jersey Office of the Secretary of Higher Education and other designated state agencies.

Training requirements for institutional staff include initial certification programs and ongoing professional development opportunities focusing on veterans' issues, trauma-informed practices, and benefit administration procedures. Staff must demonstrate competency in understanding military culture, translating military experience into academic credit, and connecting veteran students with comprehensive support services.

The regulation emphasizes the importance of creating veteran-friendly campus environments that recognize the unique needs and experiences of military-connected students. This includes providing flexible scheduling options, credit for military training and experience, and connections to mental health and counseling services specifically trained in addressing veteran-related concerns.
enhanced.summary: N.J.S.A. 18A:62-6 establishes tuition benefits for qualified New Jersey veterans and their dependents at state institutions of higher education. The program covers full tuition and fees at public institutions, with equivalent support at private colleges. Eligible participants include honorably discharged veterans who were New Jersey residents upon military entry, plus certain dependents of deceased or missing service members. Institutions must designate certified veterans' education officials, maintain comprehensive records, verify student eligibility and academic progress, coordinate with federal benefits, and provide veteran-supportive campus environments and services.
requirements: Designate certified veterans' education officials trained by the State Approving Agency to administer benefit programs and maintain current certification
Establish application procedures requiring DD-214 documentation, residency proof, and benefit applications submitted 60 days prior to term enrollment
Verify student eligibility, academic progress, and enrollment status each semester while ensuring coordination with federal GI Bill benefits
Maintain comprehensive student records including eligibility documentation, enrollment verification, and benefit payment records for minimum five years
Provide appeal procedures with due process protections for benefit denials, suspensions, or terminations, including written notification and hearing opportunities

reportingRequirements.timeline: Quarterly enrollment and benefit utilization reports due 30 days after each term's end, annual program evaluation reports including veteran student success metrics due by July 31st, and immediate notification of any eligibility determination appeals or benefit payment discrepancies to the New Jersey Office of the Secretary of Higher Education
